speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Midgut Volvulus. The combination of bilious vomiting, feeding intolerance within six hours of life, failure to pass meconium (implied by vomiting), and a family history of congenital anomalies strongly suggests intestinal malrotation with volvulus, which is a surgical emergency. Immediate surgical consultation and an abdominal X-ray are required.
